headline: Four changes are live. Mock exams draw unseen questions first and say how many are new. 17 crawlable pages cover the EU acts and texts beyond the AI Act. The first 2 engineering questions are verified against public texts. A 390 px pass brought every control on the primary screens to 44 px, with an e2e guard. IndexNow accepted all 70 sitemap URLs. One control the guard couldn't see (the sign-in button, which renders only when Supabase is configured) is fixed in the hand-back PR.
remains: When a candidate's own AI assistant can explain the AI Act in general terms, what remains here is: 141 answers checked word for word in CI against pinned official texts, including the Digital Omnibus 2026/1744, which postdates most models' training; the paper's real shape (30 questions in 40 minutes, 10 per Annex II category, mocks from unseen questions, the ranking rule from the notice); and the method (retrieval before reading, first-try calibration, spaced review of mistakes).

decisions.question: How to fill a group of the exam whose unseen questions run out
decisions.default_taken: Random from the answered questions in that group, so it is still 10 per group
decisions.why: The mock measures and doesn't drill, so weighting toward weak spots would bias the score.

decisions.question: Where the unseen count shows
decisions.default_taken: On the exam card on the Practice tab, and as start_exam.unseen
decisions.why: The candidate sees it before starting, and the likely-score check can filter to mocks that were really new.

decisions.question: Which texts get an /acts/ page
decisions.default_taken: Every pinned text that at least 2 verified questions cite (17 today). The AI Act and the Omnibus keep their /ai-act/ article pages
decisions.why: No single-question thin pages. ACT_PAGE_MIN is one constant.

decisions.question: What to call texts that aren't acts (IASR, the GPAI Code, the EDPB opinion, the JRC)
decisions.default_taken: 'EU acts and texts', with the header link 'Other EU texts'
decisions.why: From the review: 'EU acts' overstated what some of the pages are.

decisions.question: Service-worker fallback for static pages
decisions.default_taken: The prefixes live in one module (src/seo/routes.ts), and a test checks every prerendered page is covered
decisions.why: The hand-kept list missed /acts/; the review caught it before merge.

decisions.question: Engineering verification bar
decisions.default_taken: The same bar as governance and policy: the passage alone must settle the key against the strongest distractor, confirmed by a quotes-only reviewer. 2 of 80 passed, and Q51 (model card) was dropped
decisions.why: Engineering questions are mostly practice judgments. Forcing citations onto them would break the 'sources dressed up' refusal in SIGNATURE.md.

decisions.question: Engineering category page once some questions are verified
decisions.default_taken: The verified questions first, topped up to 20 with the labelled sample
decisions.why: Otherwise the page would have shrunk from 20 questions to 2.

decisions.question: Tap-target rule
decisions.default_taken: 44 px for every control on the primary screens. Links in running text are exempt only when marked data-inline
decisions.why: An explicit marker can't silently hide a stand-alone link, which the first version of the guard did.

decisions.question: Option order on resume (follow-up to 2026-11-02)
decisions.default_taken: No change. The 2 Nov hand-back said options are fixed A–D; in fact merge.mjs serves a fixed shuffle per question id. That order is the same on every build, so a resumed round still shows the same options
decisions.why: A correction to the record; behaviour was right.

proposals.title: Engineering verification: where to stop
proposals.question: Should the engineering category stay mostly unverified, labelled as practice judgment, or should we pin more open texts to verify further?
options: A: stop at 2 and say on the engineering page that these are practice judgments
B: pin more openly licensed engineering texts (for example Google's 'Rules of ML', CC BY 4.0) and run another pass
proposals.recommendation: A. The exam tests judgment here, and a citation that only touches the topic would look like evidence without being any.
proposals.cost: A: one sentence on the page. B: about a day per 10 to 15 questions, with no guarantee that many pass the bar.
